title: Trent: remission and adoption free; no preceding works merit
source_text: XXXI. Nec etiam, quod inde consequens est, ullus est Doctorum Ecclesiae Rom. qui non agnoscat nos omnes apud Deum egere remissione peccatorum, ut possimus mortem aeternam vitare, & adoptari in Dei filios, ac vitae aeternae haeredes: illam vero remissionem & adoptionem in filios Dei respectu nostri gratuitam esse, nec ullis nostris operibus deberi. Id expresse docet ipsum Concilium Tridentinum, Sess. 6. cap. 8. declarans, Nos ab Apostolo dici justificari gratis, quia nihil eorum quae justificationem praecedunt, sive fides, sive opera, ipsam justificationis gratiam promeretur. Nam sub justificatione remissionem peccatorum cum sanctificatione, & renovatione interioris hominis complectitur, ut videre est Sess. 6. cap. 7. Et cap. 3. ejusdem Sessionis justificationem impii describit, Translationem ab eo statu, in quo homo nascitur filius primi Adae, in statum gratiae, & adoptionis filiorum Dei, per secundum Adam Jesum Christum Salvatorem nostrum. Inde patet ex mente illius Concilii, remissionem peccatorum, & renovationem nostram, ac adoptionem in Dei filios esse beneficia quae nobis a Deo gratis conceduntur, & quae nulla nostra opera promerentur.
pass_a_gloss: Nor, what follows thence, is there any doctor of the Roman Church who does not acknowledge that we all need remission of sins before God in order to avoid eternal death and be adopted as God’s children and heirs of eternal life; and that that remission and adoption into God’s children is gratuitous with respect to us and owed to none of our works. The Council of Trent itself expressly teaches this, Sess. 6, ch. 8, declaring that we are said by the Apostle to be justified freely, because nothing of those things that precede justification—whether faith or works—merits the grace of justification itself. For under justification it embraces remission of sins together with sanctification and renovation of the inner man, as is to be seen in Sess. 6, ch. 7. And ch. 3 of the same Session describes the justification of the ungodly as a translation from that state in which man is born a son of the first Adam into the state of grace and of the adoption of God’s children through the second Adam, Jesus Christ our Savior. Hence it is plain from that Council’s mind that remission of sins, our renovation, and adoption as God’s children are benefits granted us freely by God, which no works of ours merit.
pass_b_english: Rome too: all need free remission and adoption; Trent Sess. 6.8—nothing preceding merits justifying grace.
Justification includes remission plus sanctifying renovation; benefits are gratis.
